facts.text: Swedish pioneers settled around 1867 in what became Old Kiron, establishing a rural community in Crawford County.
The Chicago and North Western Railway built the Mondamin branch line through Crawford County, prompting Kiron's establishment at its current location in 1899.
Kiron's name came from a misspelled Kidron Valley, with the "D" omitted during early settlement.
The town became the first station west of Boyer, enabling efficient shipment of local grain, livestock, and farm produce to broader markets.
Kiron's modest median household income of $50,781 in 2022 reflects its agrarian focus, with residents keeping traditions like coffee socials and council governance in a 100% rural setting.
